prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1211; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a vehicle that entered the intersection on a red signal per the claimant's statement. Claimant reports neck and back strain and was transported to urgent care. Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Initial contact made by phone; claimant agreed to submit photos and the police report number.

Entry 2: Police report obtained. Responding officer documented damage to the driver door and rear quarter panel of the claimant's vehicle and noted both drivers gave consistent accounts of the signal phase. Other driver's insurer has been notified and has assigned a separate claim for liability review. Vehicle inspection scheduled at the body shop of the claimant's choosing.

Entry 3: Claimant provided urgent care discharge notes diagnosing cervical and lumbar strain with recommended rest, over-the-counter pain relief, and follow-up with a primary care provider if symptoms persist. Claimant reports stiffness when turning the head and lower back soreness after sitting for long periods. Advised claimant of the right to choose their own treating providers and that medical records will be requested with signed authorization.

Entry 4: Vehicle inspection completed. Estimator confirmed structural damage to the driver side frame rail and door intrusion beyond the initial photos. Vehicle is declared a repairable total pending supplement review. Rental coverage explained to claimant, who has elected a rental vehicle for the repair period. Claimant asked general questions about how injury and property damage are handled separately; explained the general process without offering a valuation.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Reports neck and back symptoms are improving but not fully resolved. Primary care follow-up scheduled. Requested signed medical authorization and wage information in case of lost time. Reminded claimant that they may consult an attorney at any time. File remains open pending medical records, repair supplement, and the other carrier's liability position.
